title: kv-cache: adaptive memory manager and eviction heuristics to reduce fragmentation, paging and spillover
author: Avery Chen
description: Context: KV cache memory pressure has been a recurring source of latency spikes and OOMs for long-running inference workloads. Root causes observed in production include fragmentation of variable-size KV entries, excessive paging when active worksets exceed contiguous allocation bounds, and uncontrolled spillover to host memory under high concurrencies which increases latency variability. Motivation: Reduce end-to-end p99 latency and OOM frequency by improving in-GPU memory utilization and providing deterministic spillover behavior under pressure. Goals: 1) Introduce an adaptive memory manager that coalesces free segments and places variable-length KV entries to reduce fragmentation; 2) Implement an LRU+frequency hybrid eviction policy that prioritizes eviction of cold, fragmented ranges and prefers compactable entries to minimize future fragmentation; 3) Add a controlled paging/spillover mechanism which batches host spills to amortize PCIe cost and exposes a configurable SLO-aware spill threshold; 4) Integrate with runtime scheduler so batching/scheduling decisions are aware of current KV memory headroom. Changes: - New component pkg/runtime/kvmanager: adaptive segment coalescer, compactable-entry detection, and compact-on-evict pathways. - Eviction policy refactor in pkg/runtime/kvcache: replaced simple LRU with LRU+LFU hybrid and eviction scoring that includes fragmentation penalty and PCIe spill cost estimate. - Paging/spillover subsystem in pkg/runtime/spillover: async batched spill writer, progress-tracking metrics, and backpressure signals to scheduler. - Scheduler hooks in runtime/scheduler to throttle continuous batching when KV headroom falls below thresholds and to favor requests that will reuse cached prefixes. - New metrics and tracing: kv.memory.used_bytes, kv.memory.fragmentation_ratio, kv.evictions.reason, kv.spill.batch_size, kv.spill.latency_p50/p95/p99. Rollout and safety: Feature gated behind runtime config kv.enable_adaptive_manager=false by default. Gradual rollout via canary on Dedicated pools with a 10% traffic ring. Observability and rollback hooks were added. Tests and benchmarks: Unit tests for allocation/coalescer, property tests to validate no-data-loss compaction, integration tests with simulated host-spill under heavy concurrency. Microbenchmarks show a 25% reduction in fragmentation_ratio and an average 12% decrease in p99 latency for long-context workloads; worst-case PCIe spill latency reduced by batching amortization. Backwards compatibility: On/off flag preserves previous behavior. API surface unchanged. See release notes and migration notes below for config knobs and recommended defaults.

review_comments: Diego Rivera (reviewer): Overall direction LGTM. Two asks: 1) add a strong invariant test that validates compaction preserves pointers for live sessions, 2) clarify the spill retry/backoff behavior in the presence of transient PCIe errors.

Avery Chen (author reply): Added property-based invariant test in tests/integration/kv_compaction_invariant_test.go and implemented exponential backoff with capped retries for spill writer; documented behavior in spill_writer.go comments.

Priya Nambiar (reviewer): Can you add a metric for 'eviction_compact_success' to track how often compaction succeeds to justify the added cost? Also please ensure the scheduler backpressure only affects continuous batching, not individual low-latency requests.

Avery Chen (author reply): Added eviction_compact_success counter and separated scheduler hooks so that single-request latency-critical paths bypass batching throttle. Updated docs with recommended thresholds.
Ethan Park (reviewer): Bench numbers look promising. Please include a short note on how this interacts with model sharding and KV reuse across shards.
Avery Chen (author reply): Added section in docs/ops/kv_memory_management.md describing shard-local caches and best practices to maximize reuse and minimize cross-shard spill.
Priya Nambiar (approve): Approved after small nits addressed.
Diego Rivera (approve): Approved. Would like to monitor kv.memory.fragmentation_ratio for next two weeks on canaries before full rollout.
ci_checks: unit-tests: initially failed (race in segment_coalescer) -> fixed -> passed
bench/perf: passed (12% p99 improvement on long-context, 25% fragmentation reduction)
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: adaptive segment coalescing, hybrid LRU+LFU eviction with fragmentation-aware scoring, and batched host spillover to reduce PCIe overhead. Reduces fragmentation and p99 latency for long-context workloads. Feature is feature-flagged and rolled out via canary.
rollout_plan: Canary 10% Dedicated pools for 7 days, monitor kv.memory.fragmentation_ratio, kv.spill.latency_p99, and kv.evictions.reason. If metrics stable, increase to 50% for 3 days then full rollout. Rollback: flip kv.enable_adaptive_manager=false.
benchmarks_summary: Long-context (8k tokens) workloads: fragmentation_ratio down 25%, p99 latency down 12% on average, tail PCIe spill latency reduced by 30% due to batching. Memory headroom variability reduced; OOMs in synthetic stress tests eliminated in 95% of runs.
notes_for_ops: Default config keeps adaptive manager disabled. Recommended thresholds: kv.spill.threshold_bytes=0.85*gpu_total_bytes, kv.compact_minitype=32 (min contiguous bytes to compact), kv.batch_spill_max_entries=256. Enable only on Dedicated pools initially.
incident_ties: SUP-4213: customer reported repeated OOMs with long-context transformer workloads; this PR addresses root causes.
docs_changes: docs/ops/kv_memory_management.md added with design, config knobs and rollout guidance
